description: Somos un equipo de Ayacucho, Perú, con experiencia en prototipos web, negocios, marketing y producción audiovisual. Desarrollamos JAMA, un proyecto en validación que conecta comercios con excedentes de alimentos y compradores. En NASA Space Apps queremos aplicar nuestras habilidades para crear una solución útil basada en datos abiertos, combinando tecnología, investigación y comunicación.
summary: KULTIVA is a decision-support tool for agricultural cooperatives in Ayacucho, Peru. It crosses NASA satellite data (temperature, frost, rainfall and vegetation) with Peru's national planting intentions and market data to compare crop rotation options for each field, showing heat, drought and frost risk, soil health and market risk. Farmers and their cooperatives see the options and choose according to their own priorities. It matters because climate extremes are already here: in Huanta, September 2026 was the hottest in 46 years (+1.58 °C above the 1991–2020 normal, NASA POWER), and when everyone plants the same crop, prices collapse.
details:
What it does: For each field, KULTIVA compares three paths (keep potato, save water with quinoa, or restore the soil with tarwi or fava beans) and shows the risk of each: heat, drought, frost, soil health and market oversupply. Farmers receive a simple sheet in plain language, printed or via WhatsApp.

How it works:

1. Looks from space: downloads NASA POWER (temperature and frost, daily since 1981), GPM IMERG (rainfall) and MODIS (vegetation).

2. Looks at the market: adds Peru's national planting intentions (ENIS, MIDAGRI) and potato arrivals and prices in Lima (EMMSA).

3. Compares with normal: measures how far 2026 is from a normal year (1991–2020) and adjusts climate to each field's altitude.

4. Compares options: agronomic rules compare three rotation paths per field; the cooperative and the farmer decide.

5. Explains simply: Gemini only writes the explanation; it never creates numbers. Every figure shows its source.

Benefits: helps cooperatives plan rotations, protect soil health and avoid market gluts.

Goal: pilot with agricultural cooperatives in Huanta, Ayacucho.

Tools: Python, React + Vite, Supabase, Vercel, Google Gemini API; AI assistants: Claude, Google Antigravity; demo video made with ChatGPT, Google Flow and Google AI Studio.
dataRefs: NASA POWER – Daily temperature (T2M, T2M_MIN, T2M_MAX), 1981–2026
GPM IMERG Late Run V07 (daily precipitation) via NASA Giovanni
MODIS MOD13Q1 v061 NDVI (250 m, 16-day) via ORNL DAAC
NASA POWER – Root-zone soil wetness (GWETROOT) and precipitation, daily
projectRefs: Copernicus DEM GLO-90 (ESA) via Open-Meteo Elevation API – plot altitude
ISRIC SoilGrids v2.0 – soil pH and texture
EMMSA/SIEA – Potato volume and price bulletin (Lima)
Marcaquispe Capiso (2021) – Thermal constant of prickly pear, UNSCH thesis
SENAMHI – Agrometeorological forecasts and frost criterion
DRA Ayacucho via Agraria.pe – 2,000+ ha lost to cold, 2024/25
Google AI Studio – AI voice-over for demo video
Claude (Anthropic) – research and code review assistant
ChatGPT – AI image generation for demo video
